claims.statement: MEXT publishes, in the statutory salary-level disclosure of a Japanese national university corporation, the model salary for age 22 as '月額 220,000円 年間給与3,634,400円' - that is, a starting salary for a university graduate of JPY 220,000 per month. This is a GROSS monthly figure. It is the '大卒初任給' (new-graduate starting salary) for the public national university sector.

MEXT publishes, in the same model-salary table, '○30歳（助教：博士修了初任給） / 月額 370,370円 年間給与6,212,766円' for a teaching assistant post at the age-30 doctoral-completion starting salary. Recorded only to show the scale spread in the same official table; note this is age 30, not an entry-level graduate salary.

assumptions: The JPY 220,000 figure is a 'monthly salary' in the Japanese sense: it is the base monthly pay (本給 plus the standard allowances that the model-salary table's 年間給与 of JPY 3,634,400 is built from), before social insurance and before income tax.

It is the public national university sector (国立大学法人), which is not the same as the much larger private-sector new-graduate market, though MEXT uses the same civil-service-linked pay scale that many Japanese employers reference.
FY2024 (令和6年度) is the salary year. It is not the 2026 tax year.
notes: THIS IS A GROSS FIGURE AND MUST NOT BE USED FOR A COST-VERSUS-SALARY BREAK-EVEN CALCULATION. In Japan, a JPY 220,000 gross monthly salary is reduced by employee social insurance (厚生年金保険料, 健康保険 and 介護保険料, 雇用保険料) and then by 源泉徴収税額, so the take-home amount is materially lower. For a genuine NET figure derived from the National Tax Agency's own 源泉徴収税額表, see 020_net_monthly_income.json in this directory. A reader would be badly misled by treating JPY 220,000 as disposable income: the tax-only component at this salary, read from the National Tax Agency's own table, is about JPY 3,840 per month, and social insurance adds a further deduction on top.
evidence_limitations: Population: model salary (モデル給与) for permanent staff of one national university corporation (国立大学法人総合研究大学院大学), disclosed to MEXT under the statutory salary-level disclosure regime. This is a single institution within one sector, and the model salary is an illustrative pay-scale point rather than an average of actual payments. It is not a survey of the Japanese private-sector new-graduate market, and MEXT's published aggregate tables for national university corporations report average annual pay for all staff and by age band, not a new-graduate starting salary. It also excludes the private sector entirely, which is where the large majority of Japanese graduates work, and it excludes the much-discussed 'job-hopping' initial salary premium.
